segments.t: Trapped in the office when Elena Pavlovna knocks, Chef Barinov ducks underneath the desk while Nagiyev speaks with her. Unaware that Barinov is hiding inches away, Elena asks Nagiyev to go easy on Viktor Petrovich once he returns from his two-week vacation.
Добрый день.
Вот так.
Слушаю вас, Елена Павловна.
Дмитрий Владимирович, у меня к вам личный разговор.
Хочу поговорить про Виктора Петровича.
Вот как.
Да ну что вы.
Подождите, в каком вы вообще смысле?
А вы в каком?
У меня к вам просьба.
Вы можете его сильно не нагружать.
А откуда вернется?
Подождите, он сказал, он вас предупредил.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Добрый день.
'Good afternoon.' Around the favor and point, Barinov sets a calm, everyday tone with Nagiyev.
Вот так.
'Just like that.' Turning from the favor to the truth, Vika keeps the exchange moving.
Слушаю вас, Елена Павловна.

'I am listening, Elena Pavlovna.' Nagiyev mentions that he is listening Elena Pavlovna so Barinov sees what is at stake. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Дмитрий Владимирович, у меня к вам личный разговор.

'Dmitry Vladimirovich, I have a personal matter to discuss with you.' Mentioning that he has a personal matter to discuss with Nagiyev moves the talk in a new direction. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Хочу поговорить про Виктора Петровича.
'I want to talk to you about Viktor Petrovich.' Vika reminds Barinov that she wants to talk to Barinov about Viktor Petrovich before the moment passes.
Вот как.
'Is that so.' Around the trip and conversation, Nagiyev sets a calm, everyday tone with Barinov.
Да ну что вы.
'Oh, come on now.' Telling Nagiyev to come on now is how Barinov lays out the situation for Nagiyev. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Подождите, в каком вы вообще смысле?
'Wait a second, in what sense do you mean that?' Asking whether a second in what sense do Barinov means puts Barinov right on the defensive.
А вы в каком?

'And in what sense did you mean it?' Wondering if in what sense did Barinov means it shows Nagiyev caught off guard. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
У меня к вам просьба.

'I have a favor to ask of you.' Realizing that he has a favor to ask of Nagiyev changes how Barinov handles the situation. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Вы можете его сильно не нагружать.
'Could you please not overload him with work when he gets back.' Since could Barinov pleases not overload him with work when he gets back, Vika does not waste words on excuses.
А откуда вернется?

'Wait, gets back from where?' With the moment and work hanging in the air, Nagiyev puts Barinov on the spot. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Подождите, он сказал, он вас предупредил.

'Hold on, he told me that he had already informed you.' Even though Nagiyev should hold on he told him that he had already informed Nagiyev, Barinov keeps a steady face in front of Nagiyev. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Добрый день.
Вот так.
Слушаю вас, Елена Павловна.
Дмитрий Владимирович, у меня к вам личный разговор.
Хочу поговорить про Виктора Петровича.
Вот как.
Да ну что вы.
Подождите, в каком вы вообще смысле?
А вы в каком?
У меня к вам просьба.
Вы можете его сильно не нагружать.
А откуда вернется?
Подождите, он сказал, он вас предупредил.
That wraps up this scene as elena Pavlovna asks Nagiyev not to overwork Viktor Petrovich when he returns from his trip, while Chef Barinov hides underneath Nagiyev's desk. Until next time!
До свидания!
